docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
The Community Water Management System is a multi-organization platform for any body that supplies water and bills customers by meter. It helps organizations maintain customer and connection records, read meters, bill customers, collect M-Pesa payments, track operating expenses, and produce management reports.

The system is intended to replace paper-based processes, reduce manual errors, support cashless M-Pesa collections, and give managers and committees clearer financial and operational visibility.

docs.title: Who the platform serves
docs.text:
The platform is sold as a monthly subscription to organizations such as:

  • Community water schemes, for example Kituasi A and Kituasi B, often run by a committee.
  • County governments managing water across several schemes or areas.
  • Water service providers of any size.
  • Property managers and landlords who meter and bill tenants across one or more buildings.

Kituasi Project is used throughout this documentation as a worked example only. Every rule that differs between organizations (tariffs, penalties, disconnection rules, payment allocation, reading frequency) is an organization setting, not a fixed behaviour.

docs.title: Who this documentation is for
docs.text:
• The platform provider and platform administrators
  • Organization administrators, managers, and community committees
  • Field officers, meter readers, and accountants
  • Developers and technical maintainers

docs.title: Main capabilities
docs.text:
• Onboard many organizations, each running one or more schemes, with every organization's and scheme's data kept separate.
  • Bill organizations a monthly subscription based on active meters, plus SMS charged per message.
  • Register customers, manage connections and rental units, and store signed contracts.
  • Verify customers by SMS and provide self-service through a web portal and a USSD menu for basic phones.
  • Record meter readings with GPS and a meter photo, flag unusual readings, record why a meter could not be read, and work offline.
  • Compare main supply readings with water sold to estimate water loss.
  • Bill by price per unit for each connection type, with an optional standing fee for zero-usage readings.
  • Collect cashless M-Pesa payments to each scheme's own Paybill, reconcile them, and send SMS receipts.
  • Apply configurable penalties, disconnection, and reconnection rules.
  • Track customer problem reports through to resolution.
  • Record expenses with custom categories and receipts, and record donor or government funding.
  • Send bills, receipts, reminders, and bulk notices by SMS.
  • Import existing customers, meters, readings, and balances from an Excel template.
  • Produce internal reports exportable to PDF and Excel.

docs.title: Documentation map
docs.text:
• Requirements describes expected system capabilities and business rules.
  • Workflows describes the main processes from the user's perspective.
  • Architecture lists technical design decisions that are still open.
  • Development contains setup and maintenance instructions as the implementation is established.

docs.title: Scope note
docs.text: This documentation started from the supplied Project Operations & Requirements Guide: Community Water Management System and has been extended through requirements sessions with the product owner. Where a rule is not yet agreed, it is listed under "Questions to confirm" rather than treated as a requirement.

docs.title: Status
docs.text: To be defined. The business requirements are documented; the technology stack and system architecture have not yet been chosen.

docs.title: Decisions to document
docs.text:
• Web, mobile, or progressive web application approach for staff and customers
  • Frontend and backend technologies
  • Database technology and the multi-tenant strategy for keeping organizations and schemes separate
  • Authentication, SMS verification, role-based access control, and password recovery
  • M-Pesa integration provider, per-scheme Paybill configuration, callbacks, duplicate transaction handling, and reconciliation
  • SMS provider, sender names per organization, delivery handling, and per-message counting for billing
  • USSD provider, shared USSD code, and session handling
  • Platform subscription billing: monthly active-meter counts, invoicing, and read-only mode for unpaid organizations
  • Offline storage and synchronization of meter readings and photos
  • GPS capture, map provider, and location-data access controls
  • File storage for contracts, meter photos, and receipts
  • Excel import and PDF/Excel report export
  • Audit logging and data retention
  • Hosting, deployment, backups, monitoring, and disaster recovery

docs.title: Architecture principles from the requirements
docs.text:
• Data isolation. No organization can access another's data. Within an organization, customer lists, bills, and ledgers are scoped to schemes, and staff access is scoped to assigned schemes. The design must show how this is enforced on every operation.
  • Configuration over code. Tariffs, standing fees, reading frequency, payment allocation order, and penalty and disconnection rules are organization settings.
  • Payments never blocked. Customer M-Pesa payments, allocation, and receipts must keep working even when an organization's subscription is unpaid.
  • Offline-first field work. Meter reading must work without network coverage.
  • Basic phone support. Core customer actions must be available through SMS and USSD, not only the web portal.

docs.title: Status
docs.text: To be completed once the implementation stack and repository are known. The project requirements PDF does not specify application dependencies or runtime requirements.

docs.title: Application setup details to add
docs.text:
• Required language and runtime versions
  • Dependency installation commands
  • Environment variables and example configuration

Do not add real passwords, API keys, M-Pesa secrets, or other credentials to the documentation repository.

docs.title: Tariff settings
docs.text:
Each organization sets:

  • A price per unit for each connection type. For example, a business or kiosk that resells water may pay a lower price per unit than a household.
  • An optional standing fee.
  • A flat monthly amount for Flat Rate connections, which have no meter reading.
  • A due date rule, for example a set number of days after the bill is issued.

docs.title: How a bill is calculated
docs.text:
units used    = current reading − previous real reading
water charge  = units used × price per unit for the connection type
bill          = water charge (or standing fee) + other charges due

docs.title: Standing fee
docs.text:
The standing fee applies only when a reading is taken and shows 0 units used.

Situation Charge Reading taken, usage 0 Standing fee Reading taken, usage above 0 Units × price only, with no standing fee, even if that is less than the standing fee No reading (blank period) Nothing

Example (standing fee KES 100, price KES 50 per unit):

Month Reading Usage Bill January 105 5 KES 250 February 105 0 KES 100 (standing fee) March — blank Nothing April 108 3 (since February) KES 150

docs.title: Other charges
docs.text: Fines, penalties, reconnection fees, and connection fees are added to the customer's account as separate charges. See Penalties, disconnection, and reconnection.

docs.title: Bills
docs.text:
• A bill is produced when a reading is recorded for the billing period.
  • Every bill shows previous reading, current reading, units used, charges, previous balance, total due, due date, the scheme's Paybill, and the customer's account number.
  • Bills are sent by SMS and are visible in the portal and through USSD.
  • Disconnected and suspended connections are not billed.

docs.title: Opening balances
docs.text: Balances owed or held in credit before an organization joined the platform are imported as opening balances. See Data import.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• BL-01 — Price per connection type: Each organization sets a price per unit for each connection type.
  • BL-02 — Usage-based bill: Bills are units used multiplied by the price for the connection type.
  • BL-03 — Standing fee: If enabled, the standing fee is charged only when a recorded reading shows zero usage.
  • BL-04 — No minimum charge: When usage is above zero, only usage is charged, even if it is less than the standing fee.
  • BL-05 — Blank periods: Periods without a reading produce no bill and no standing fee.
  • BL-06 — Flat rate: Flat Rate connections are billed a fixed amount without readings.
  • BL-07 — Bill content: Bills include readings, units, charges, balance, due date, Paybill, and account number.
  • BL-08 — Bill delivery: Bills are sent by SMS and available in the portal and USSD.
  • BL-09 — Bill adjustment: A corrected reading adjusts the related bill, with an audit trail.

docs.title: Questions to confirm
docs.text:
• Are Flat Rate connections billed every month, even when other meters are not read?
  • Can tariffs change mid-year, and does a new price apply from a date or from the next reading?
  • Should a bill covering several months (after blank periods) be split by month for reporting?
  • Is VAT or any other tax added to water bills for any organization type?

docs.title: Language
docs.text: All SMS, USSD menus, and portal screens are in English only.

docs.title: SMS
docs.text:
Every SMS is charged to the organization per message (see Platform administration). Messages are sent under the organization's own sender name.

Message When Verification code Customer account created Bill Bill produced after a reading Payment receipt Payment matched Reminder Before the due date and on becoming overdue, if enabled Disconnection warning Before a disconnection visit Problem report update Report assigned and resolved Bulk notice Sent by a manager or org admin

docs.title: Bulk notices
docs.text:
A manager or org admin can send a notice, for example "Water will be off on Thursday for repairs", to:

  • A whole scheme
  • One zone, route, or building
  • One connection type

Before sending, the system shows the number of messages and the cost.

docs.title: USSD
docs.text:
Customers with basic phones use a USSD menu. The customer is identified by their phone number, so the same menu works for every organization.

Menu option Result Check balance Current balance and due date Last bill Readings, units, and amount of the latest bill Pay Sends an M-Pesa PIN prompt to the phone Report a problem Choose a problem type; the report is created

docs.title: Web portal
docs.text: Customers with smartphones or computers use the portal. See Customer management for portal features.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• CM-01 — Transactional SMS: The system sends the messages listed above.
  • CM-02 — Sender name: SMS are sent under the organization's sender name.
  • CM-03 — Bulk notices: Managers and org admins can send notices to a scheme, zone, building, or connection type.
  • CM-04 — Cost preview: Bulk notices show message count and cost before sending.
  • CM-05 — SMS charging: All SMS are counted per organization for billing.
  • CM-06 — USSD menu: Customers can check balance, see their last bill, pay, and report a problem by USSD.
  • CM-07 — English only: All customer-facing text is in English.

docs.title: Questions to confirm
docs.text:
• Is one USSD code shared by all organizations on the platform?
  • How does USSD handle a phone number linked to more than one account?
  • Who pays for USSD session costs: the customer, the organization, or the platform?
  • Can customers opt out of reminders or bulk notices?

docs.title: Customer data
docs.text:
Field Notes Full name Required Mobile phone number Required; used for SMS, USSD, M-Pesa, and portal login National ID number Required for community, county, and provider schemes; optional for tenants Member number Community schemes only Registration date Required Account (connection) number Generated; used as the M-Pesa account number

Fields that only apply to some organization types are optional for the others.

docs.title: Connection profile
docs.text:
• Meter serial number
  • Connection type: Household, Business, School/Institution, Kiosk, Bowser, or Flat Rate. Each type can have its own price per unit (see Billing and tariffs).
  • Zone, route, or building and unit
  • GPS location of the meter
  • Connection status:
Status Meaning Applied Application recorded; not yet connected Active Connected and billed Suspended Temporarily stopped at the customer's request, for example while away Disconnected Stopped by the organization, usually for non-payment

Kiosks and bowsers are treated like any other connection: their meter is read and billed. How they resell water is not tracked.

docs.title: New connection (community, county, and provider schemes)
docs.text:
1. Applied: the customer applies and their details are recorded.
  2. Fee paid: the connection fee is paid by M-Pesa.
  3. Contract signed: the user agreement and, where required, land consent form are signed and uploaded.
  4. Installed: the field officer installs the meter and records its serial number, starting reading, and GPS location.
  5. Active: billing starts from the starting reading.

A connection cannot be activated until the connection fee is paid and the contract is uploaded.

See Customer registration workflow.

docs.title: Rental units (property managers)
docs.text:
• The meter belongs to the unit, not the tenant.
  • A tenant moves into a unit. There is no application, connection fee, or water contract.
  • A move-in reading is taken so the new tenant is not billed for earlier usage.
  • A move-out reading produces a final bill. Any unpaid amount stays with the outgoing tenant's account, not the unit.
  • Credit left after the final bill is refunded to the tenant (see M-Pesa payments).
  • While a unit is empty, its water is billed to the landlord.
  • Each meter keeps a history of account holders over time.

See Tenant move-in and move-out workflow.

docs.title: Contract documents
docs.text:
• Scanned photos or PDF copies of signed user agreements and land consent forms can be uploaded.
  • Accounts missing required signed contracts are flagged.
  • Customers can view their signed contract in the portal.
  • Contracts do not apply to tenants of property managers.

docs.title: Customer account verification
docs.text:
• Field staff attach a new customer to their scheme.
  • The system creates a customer account linked to the mobile phone number.
  • The customer receives an SMS verification code, uses it to verify their identity, and sets a password.

docs.title: Customer self-service
docs.text:
Customers use the web portal (smartphone or computer) or the USSD menu (any phone). See Customer communication.

Feature Portal USSD View current bill and balance Yes Yes View past consumption and readings, including meter photos Yes Last bill only Pay through M-Pesa Yes Yes View signed contract Yes No Report a problem Yes Yes

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• CU-01 — Register customer: Field officers can record customer and connection details against a scheme.
  • CU-02 — Optional fields by organization type: Fields that do not apply to an organization type are optional.
  • CU-03 — Connection status: Connections move through Applied, Active, Suspended, and Disconnected.
  • CU-04 — Activation checks: A new connection cannot be activated until the connection fee is paid and the contract is uploaded (not applicable to rental units).
  • CU-05 — Contract upload: Signed documents can be uploaded and missing ones flagged.
  • CU-06 — Tenant occupancy: A tenant can be moved into and out of a unit, with move-in and move-out readings.
  • CU-07 — Final bill: A move-out reading produces a final bill on the outgoing tenant's account.
  • CU-08 — Empty unit billing: Usage on an empty unit is billed to the landlord.
  • CU-09 — Account holder history: Each meter keeps a history of its account holders.
  • CU-10 — SMS verification: A customer can verify their account by SMS code and set a password.
  • CU-11 — Own data only: Customers can only view their own account information.

docs.title: Acceptance criteria
docs.text:
• A customer record is associated with the correct scheme.
  • A new community connection cannot become Active without a paid fee and uploaded contract.
  • A tenant moving in is not billed for usage before their move-in reading.
  • An empty unit's usage appears on the landlord's account.
  • A customer can complete SMS verification and set a password.

docs.title: Questions to confirm
docs.text:
• Must National ID numbers be unique across the platform, within an organization, or within a scheme?
  • Can one customer have multiple connections or meters, and do they share one balance?
  • What is the required document list for each connection type?
  • What happens when a customer changes their phone number or cannot receive an SMS?
  • Is the landlord a customer account within the scheme, or a separate type of record?

docs.title: Description
docs.text: When an organization joins, its existing records are on paper or in Excel. Records are brought in using an Excel template during onboarding.

docs.title: Template contents
docs.text: Data Columns Customers Name, phone number, National ID (where applicable), member number (where applicable) Connections Account number, connection type, scheme, zone or building and unit, status Meters Serial number, last reading and its date Balances Opening balance: amount owed or credit held

docs.title: Process
docs.text:
1. The org admin, or the platform admin on their behalf, downloads the template.
  2. The organization fills it in and uploads it.
  3. The system checks the file and lists every problem, such as a missing phone number, duplicate meter, unknown connection type, or text where a number is expected.
  4. Nothing is saved until the file has no errors.
  5. Once clean, the records are created.

docs.title: Effects of the import
docs.text:
• Last reading becomes the starting point. The first bill in the system is the next reading minus the imported last reading.
  • Opening balances become the first entry on each account. Amounts owed are treated as overdue bills under the payment allocation order; credit is applied to the next bill.
  • Contracts and documents are not imported. They are uploaded afterwards, and missing ones appear in the customer compliance report.

The import can be run again later, for example when a property manager adds a building or a county takes over another scheme.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• DI-01 — Template download: A standard Excel template is available.
  • DI-02 — Validation: Uploaded files are checked and all errors listed.
  • DI-03 — All or nothing: No records are saved until the file is free of errors.
  • DI-04 — Starting readings: Imported last readings are used as the previous reading for the first bill.
  • DI-05 — Opening balances: Imported balances are recorded as the first account entry.
  • DI-06 — Repeat imports: Imports can be run after onboarding to add new customers.
  • DI-07 — Who can import: Org admins and platform admins can run imports.

docs.title: Questions to confirm
docs.text:
• Should an import be able to update existing records, or only add new ones?
  • Is historical reading and payment history imported, or only the latest reading and balance?
  • Should imported accounts start verified, or must every customer complete SMS verification?

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Organizations handle non-payment differently. Kituasi, for example, has no late penalties and no disconnection deadline. Every rule on this page is an organization setting and is off by default.

docs.title: Organization settings
docs.text: Setting Options Late penalty On/off; fixed amount or percentage of the overdue bill; number of days after the due date Disconnection rule On/off; account becomes eligible when overdue by a set number of days or a set amount Reconnection fee Amount charged to reconnect Reminder SMS On/off; days before the due date; on becoming overdue

docs.title: Disconnection
docs.text:
1. Accounts meeting the disconnection rule appear on the field action list, grouped by zone.
  2. A manager approves each disconnection. No customer is disconnected automatically.
  3. The customer receives a warning SMS before the visit.
  4. The field officer disconnects, records the meter reading and a photo, and the connection becomes Disconnected.

docs.title: Reconnection
docs.text:
1. The customer pays the overdue amount and the reconnection fee.
  2. The account appears on the field officer's reconnection list.
  3. The field officer reconnects and records the meter reading.
  4. The connection returns to Active.

docs.title: Fines
docs.text: A manager can add a one-off fine, for example for an illegal connection or meter tampering. Fines are separate from late penalties, are logged, and are paid first under the payment allocation order.

docs.title: Suspension
docs.text: Suspended means a temporary stop at the customer's request, for example while away. A suspended connection is not billed and is not counted for the organization's subscription. It is not used for non-payment.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• DC-01 — Configurable penalties: Late penalties can be enabled per organization as a fixed amount or percentage.
  • DC-02 — Configurable disconnection rule: Disconnection eligibility is configured per organization by days or amount overdue.
  • DC-03 — Field action list: Eligible accounts are listed by zone.
  • DC-04 — Manager approval: Disconnections require manager approval.
  • DC-05 — Warning SMS: Customers are warned by SMS before disconnection.
  • DC-06 — Disconnection record: Disconnections record the reading, photo, field officer, and date.
  • DC-07 — Reconnection: Paying the overdue amount and reconnection fee places the account on the reconnection list.
  • DC-08 — Fines: Managers can add logged one-off fines.
  • DC-09 — Customer suspension: A connection can be suspended and resumed at the customer's request.
  • DC-10 — Reminder SMS: Organizations can enable due-date and overdue reminders.

docs.title: Questions to confirm
docs.text:
• Can a manager waive a penalty, fine, or reconnection fee, and is that logged?
  • Should a customer on a payment plan be excluded from the field action list?
  • Is there a maximum period a connection can stay Suspended?
  • Does a suspension need a reading at the start and the end?

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: The system records operating expenses and non-customer funding so each scheme can understand its running costs and prepare financial reports.

docs.title: Recording expenses
docs.text:
• The accountant records expenses against a scheme.
  • Expenses are approved by the committee in its meetings, outside the system. The accountant records an expense after it is approved.
  • Each expense has:
    • Date
    • Category
    • Amount
    • Quantity and unit where applicable (litres of diesel, kilograms of chlorine)
    • Payment method (M-Pesa, bank, or cheque)
    • Optional approval reference, such as the meeting date or minute number
    • Optional receipt upload (photo or PDF)
  • A wrong expense is edited or cancelled, never deleted. Every change is logged.

docs.title: Expense categories
docs.text: The system provides default categories. Each organization can add its own custom categories, for example bulk water bills for a property manager.

docs.title: Default categories
docs.text: Category Examples Pumping and fuel Diesel for pumps or generators, power units Water treatment Chlorine, soda ash, other chemicals Maintenance and repairs Pipe burst repairs, fittings, engine servicing, pump spare parts Staff salaries Payroll Office costs Rent, stationery, airtime, transport, meeting allowances, audit fees

docs.title: Donor and government funding
docs.text: The accountant records funding that does not come from customers, with source (donor, county, NGO, or other), amount, date, and purpose. Funding is reported separately from customer collections.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• EX-01 — Record expenses: The accountant records expenses against a scheme.
  • EX-02 — Categorize expenses: Expenses use default or organization-defined categories.
  • EX-03 — Custom categories: Org admins can add expense categories.
  • EX-04 — Quantities and costs: Quantity and unit can be stored alongside cost.
  • EX-05 — Receipt upload: A receipt photo or PDF can be attached.
  • EX-06 — Approval reference: An optional committee approval reference can be recorded.
  • EX-07 — No deletion: Expenses are edited or cancelled with an audit trail, not deleted.
  • EX-08 — Funding: Donor and government funding can be recorded separately from customer income.
  • EX-09 — Reporting: Expenses and funding are included in financial reports and the profit and loss statement.

docs.title: Questions to confirm
docs.text:
• Which currency, tax treatment, and accounting period should be used?
  • How should recurring costs such as salaries and rent be entered: monthly by hand or as a repeating entry?
  • Can an expense be shared across several schemes in one organization?

docs.title: Reading frequency
docs.text:
Each organization sets how often it reads meters. Some read every month; others skip months. A reading period without a reading is blank:

  • No bill is produced for a blank period.
  • No standing fee is charged for a blank period.
  • Usage is never estimated.
  • The next real reading covers all units used since the last real reading.

Example: January is read. February and March are blank. April is read. The April bill charges all units used from the January reading to the April reading.

docs.title: Taking a reading
docs.text:
1. The meter reader opens the app and selects an assigned route.
  2. The app shows each meter's previous reading.
  3. The reader enters the current reading and takes a photo of the meter.
  4. The app captures GPS coordinates when location permission is granted.
  5. The system flags a reading that is lower than the previous reading or an unusually large increase. The reader reviews the warning before submitting.
  6. Without network coverage, readings and photos are saved on the phone and synchronized when connectivity returns.

docs.title: Meters that cannot be read
docs.text:
When a meter cannot be read, the reader records a "not read" reason instead of a number, such as:

  • Locked gate or no access
  • Meter broken or damaged
  • Meter buried or obstructed
  • Customer absent (where access requires them)
  • Other, with a note

Unread meters and their reasons are shown in the unread meters report. Meters left blank several periods in a row are highlighted for follow-up.

docs.title: Meter problems
docs.text:
• Meter replaced: the old meter's final reading and the new meter's starting reading are both recorded, so usage is not overstated.
  • Meter rollover: a reading that wrapped past the meter's maximum (for example 9999 to 0000) is flagged for a manager to confirm. It is never billed as negative usage.
  • Wrong reading: a manager can correct it. The original value, new value, who changed it, and why are logged. If the reading was already billed, the bill is adjusted.

docs.title: Main supply meter
docs.text: Readers also record readings at the main source meter, such as a pumping station or tank. The system compares water supplied with water sold to estimate water lost through leaks or illegal connections.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• MR-01 — Route assignment: Readers see only their assigned routes.
  • MR-02 — Reading history: The previous reading is visible during data entry.
  • MR-03 — Validation: Lower-than-previous and unusually high readings are flagged.
  • MR-04 — GPS capture: Coordinates are attached to a reading when available and permitted.
  • MR-05 — Offline capture: Readings and photos can be stored offline and synchronized later.
  • MR-06 — Supply readings: Main supply meter readings are recorded separately from customer meters.
  • MR-07 — Water-loss comparison: The system compares supplied water with water sold to estimate loss.
  • MR-08 — Map view: Authorized managers can view meter locations on a map.
  • MR-09 — Meter photo: Each reading includes a photo of the meter, visible to managers and the customer.
  • MR-10 — Reading frequency setting: Each organization configures how often meters are read.
  • MR-11 — Not-read reason: A reader can record why a meter was not read instead of entering a reading.
  • MR-12 — No estimates: Missing readings are never estimated; the next real reading covers the whole gap.
  • MR-13 — Meter replacement: Replacing a meter records the old final reading and the new starting reading.
  • MR-14 — Rollover handling: Rollovers are flagged for manager confirmation.
  • MR-15 — Reading correction: Managers can correct readings, with an audit trail.

docs.title: Questions to confirm
docs.text:
• What counts as an "unusually high" increase, and should the threshold vary by connection type?
  • How should conflicting offline edits be resolved?
  • Is the unit always cubic metres, or can an organization use litres?
  • Is a meter photo mandatory for every reading, or only when the reading is flagged?
  • What exact formula and reporting period should be used for water loss?

docs.title: Description
docs.text: An organization subscribes to the platform and runs one or more schemes. Examples: Kituasi community runs Kituasi A and Kituasi B; a county runs several rural schemes; a property manager runs several apartment estates. Each scheme's customers, bills, and ledger are kept separate from other schemes and from other organizations.

docs.title: Organization setup
docs.text:
The org admin configures:

  • Organization name, type (community scheme, county, water service provider, property manager), and SMS sender name
  • Schemes and their administrative locations: County, Sub-County, Ward, Location, and Village
  • Zones, routes, or buildings within each scheme
  • One M-Pesa Paybill per scheme, so customer payments go directly to that scheme
  • Tariffs: price per unit for each connection type, and the optional standing fee (see Billing and tariffs)
  • Meter-reading frequency (see Meter reading)
  • Payment allocation order (see M-Pesa payments)
  • Penalty, disconnection, reconnection, and reminder rules (see Penalties, disconnection, and reconnection)
  • Expense categories (see Expenses and funding)
  • Staff and their roles and scheme assignments (see Roles and permissions)

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• OS-01 — Create a scheme: An org admin can create schemes within their organization.
  • OS-02 — Configure locations: County, Sub-County, Ward, Location, and Village data are defined for each scheme.
  • OS-03 — Zones and buildings: A scheme can be divided into zones, routes, or buildings.
  • OS-04 — Paybill per scheme: Each scheme has its own M-Pesa Paybill.
  • OS-05 — Isolate organization data: No organization can see another organization's data.
  • OS-06 — Isolate scheme data: Customer lists, bills, and ledgers of one scheme are not mixed with another scheme's.
  • OS-07 — Assign staff: Staff are assigned to the schemes they may access.
  • OS-08 — Restrict access: Staff only view and manage data for their assigned schemes; the org admin sees all schemes in the organization.
  • OS-09 — Organization-wide view: An organization with several schemes can see them side by side in reports.
  • OS-10 — Per-organization settings: Tariffs and policies are configured per organization and do not affect other organizations.

docs.title: Acceptance criteria
docs.text:
• A scheme can be created with its administrative location hierarchy and Paybill.
  • A staff member assigned to one scheme cannot access another scheme's customer records, bills, or ledger.
  • No user of one organization can access any data of another organization.
  • Reports and lists are scoped to the selected and authorized scheme or organization.

docs.title: Questions to confirm
docs.text:
• Can tariffs differ between schemes within the same organization, or are they set once per organization?
  • Can location records be edited after a scheme has started operating?
  • Can a scheme be moved from one organization to another (for example, when a county takes over a community scheme)?

docs.title: Problem statement
docs.text: Organizations that supply water — community schemes, counties, water service providers, and property managers — need accurate customer and meter records, timely bill collection, and clear expense tracking. Paper-based processes introduce manual errors and make it difficult to reconcile collections or understand a scheme's financial position.

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Provide one platform that many independent water organizations can subscribe to.
  2. Centralize customer, connection, meter, billing, payment, and expense records for each organization.
  3. Keep each organization's and each scheme's data separate.
  4. Let each organization configure its own tariffs and policies instead of hard-coding one scheme's rules.
  5. Improve the reliability and timeliness of M-Pesa payment reconciliation.
  6. Help field staff collect meter readings, including where network connectivity is unavailable.
  7. Make water production, sales, estimated losses, collections, unpaid balances, and operating costs visible to management and committees.
  8. Serve customers with smartphones (web portal) and basic phones (SMS and USSD).

docs.title: Platform structure
docs.text:
Level Description Examples Platform The product run by the platform provider. — Organization The body that subscribes to the platform. Kituasi community, a county government, a water company, a property management firm Scheme A water system run by the organization, with its own customers, Paybill, and ledger. Kituasi A, Kituasi B, a county's rural scheme, an apartment estate Zone / route / building A subdivision of a scheme used for meter reading and follow-up. Village zone, reading route, Block C

A small community may have one organization with one scheme. A county may have many schemes and needs an organization-wide view across them.

docs.title: Organization types
docs.text: Type Distinguishing features Community water scheme Often run by a committee; customers apply, pay a connection fee, and sign a contract. County government Many schemes; needs consolidated reporting. Water service provider Similar to a community scheme, possibly larger. Property manager Customers are tenants who occupy units; meters belong to units; empty units are billed to the landlord.

docs.title: User groups
docs.text:
Role Responsibilities Platform admin Onboards organizations, manages subscriptions, suspends or reactivates organizations, and provides logged support access. Org admin Configures the organization, its schemes, tariffs, and policies; manages staff. Manager Runs assigned schemes; approves disconnections and corrections; reviews readings and reports. Field officer Registers customers, installs meters, handles problem reports, disconnections, and reconnections. Meter reader Captures readings on assigned routes. Accountant Records expenses and funding, matches unmatched payments, runs financial reports. Committee member Read-only access to reports and finances. Customer Views bills and consumption, pays through M-Pesa, views contracts, and reports problems via the portal or USSD.

See Roles and permissions for detail.

docs.title: Functional areas
docs.text:
• Platform administration and subscriptions
  • Organizations and schemes
  • Roles and permissions
  • Customer management
  • Meter reading
  • Billing and tariffs
  • M-Pesa payments
  • Penalties, disconnection, and reconnection
  • Problem reports
  • Customer communication
  • Expenses and funding
  • Reports
  • Data import

docs.title: Out of scope
docs.text:
• Reports for regulators such as WASREB. Reports are for internal management only.
  • Cash collection. All payments are cashless through M-Pesa.
  • Tracking how kiosks or bowsers resell water. They are billed as ordinary meters.
  • Languages other than English.

This requirements set does not yet define the database schema, API contracts, technology stack, hosting, or security implementation. See System architecture.

docs.title: Payment channels
docs.text:
All payments are cashless, through M-Pesa only. Staff never collect cash.

  • Portal or USSD: the customer chooses to pay and receives an M-Pesa PIN prompt on their phone.
  • Direct Paybill: the customer sends money to the scheme's Paybill and enters their account number.

Each scheme has its own Paybill, so payments go directly to the scheme and never pass through the platform provider.

docs.title: Matching payments
docs.text:
1. The system receives the M-Pesa transaction.
  2. If the account number matches a customer in that scheme, the payment is recorded automatically.
  3. If the account number is wrong or missing, the payment goes to the unmatched payments list. The accountant matches it manually to the right customer. Each manual match is logged.
  4. A transaction code is recorded only once, even if M-Pesa sends the same notification more than once.
  5. The customer receives an SMS receipt with the amount, M-Pesa code, and updated balance.

docs.title: Payment allocation
docs.text:
Payments are applied in this default order:

  1. Outstanding fines
  2. Reconnection fees
  3. Past overdue bills (including imported opening balances)
  4. Current usage bill
  5. Any remaining amount is kept as account credit for the next bill

Each organization can change this order.

docs.title: Credit and refunds
docs.text:
• Credit is applied automatically to the next bill.
  • When a tenant moves out, credit is first applied to the final bill. Any remaining credit is refunded to the tenant by the accountant, outside the system, and the refund is recorded in the system.

docs.title: Revenue categories
docs.text:
Collections are reported separately as:

  • Water usage bills
  • Standing fees
  • Connection and registration fees
  • Reconnection fees
  • Fines and penalties
  • Donor and government funding (recorded by the accountant; see Expenses and funding)

Kiosks and bowsers are billed as ordinary connections, not as a separate revenue category.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• BP-01 — Portal and USSD payment: Customers can start an M-Pesa payment from the portal or USSD.
  • BP-02 — Direct payment: Payments to a scheme's Paybill are received and matched.
  • BP-03 — Paybill per scheme: Each scheme's payments go to its own Paybill.
  • BP-04 — Automatic matching: Payments with a valid account number are matched automatically.
  • BP-05 — Unmatched payments: Payments that cannot be matched are listed for the accountant to match manually, with an audit trail.
  • BP-06 — Duplicate protection: Each M-Pesa transaction code is recorded once.
  • BP-07 — Allocation: Payments are applied in the organization's configured order.
  • BP-08 — Account credit: Excess payment is kept as credit and applied to the next bill.
  • BP-09 — Refund record: Refunds made outside the system can be recorded against the account.
  • BP-10 — SMS receipt: Customers receive a receipt with amount, M-Pesa code, and updated balance.
  • BP-11 — Revenue classification: Collections can be reported by revenue category.
  • BP-12 — Unaffected by subscription status: Payments continue even if the organization's platform subscription is unpaid.

docs.title: Questions to confirm
docs.text:
• Which M-Pesa integration provider and callback method will be used?
  • How should M-Pesa reversals be handled once a payment has been allocated?
  • How long can a payment stay unmatched before it is escalated?
  • Can a customer request a refund of credit while still connected?

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The platform provider sells the system to many organizations. A platform admin manages those organizations and bills them for using the platform. The platform admin does not run any organization's day-to-day operations.

docs.title: Platform admin capabilities
docs.text:
• Create and activate a new organization and its first org admin.
  • Set and change an organization's subscription plan.
  • Generate and track subscription invoices.
  • Suspend and reactivate organizations.
  • View platform-wide usage: organizations, schemes, active meters, and SMS volume.
  • Enter an organization's data only for support purposes. Every support access is recorded in an audit log.

Outside logged support access, an organization's customer and financial data belongs to that organization and is not visible to the platform admin.

docs.title: Subscription
docs.text:
• Each organization pays a monthly subscription based on its number of active meters.
  • Disconnected and suspended meters are not counted.
  • The active meter count is taken each month and used to calculate the invoice.
  • SMS is charged per message on top of the subscription. This covers bills, receipts, reminders, verification codes, and bulk notices.
  • Subscription invoices are sent to the org admin and paid by M-Pesa or bank transfer.

docs.title: Non-payment of the subscription
docs.text:
1. Reminders are sent to the org admin before and after the due date.
  2. After a grace period, the organization becomes read-only:
    • Staff can view records and reports.
    • Staff cannot add or change data (readings, customers, expenses, and so on).
    • Customers keep paying. M-Pesa payments continue to be received, matched, and allocated, and SMS receipts continue to be sent.
  3. When the overdue amount is paid, full access is restored immediately.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• PA-01 — Onboard organization: A platform admin can create an organization and its first org admin.
  • PA-02 — Subscription plan: Each organization has a subscription priced by active meters.
  • PA-03 — Meter count: Active meters are counted monthly for billing; disconnected and suspended meters are excluded.
  • PA-04 — SMS charging: SMS sent by or for an organization are counted and charged per message.
  • PA-05 — Subscription invoices: The platform generates monthly invoices to each organization.
  • PA-06 — Read-only on non-payment: After the grace period, an unpaid organization's staff have read-only access.
  • PA-07 — Customer payments continue: Customer payments, allocation, and receipts are never blocked by an organization's subscription status.
  • PA-08 — Restore access: Paying the overdue amount restores full access.
  • PA-09 — Support access audit: Any platform admin access to an organization's data is logged with who, when, and why.
  • PA-10 — Platform usage view: Platform admins can view usage across all organizations.

docs.title: Questions to confirm
docs.text:
• Is the per-meter price a flat rate, or are there price bands (for example 1–100 meters, 101–500 meters)?
  • How long is the grace period before read-only access applies?
  • Is there a minimum monthly charge, setup fee, or free trial?
  • What is the price per SMS, and does it vary by message type?
  • How is an organization's data handled if it permanently leaves the platform (export, retention, deletion)?

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Customers report leaks and other service problems. A field officer goes to fix them, and the customer is kept informed.

docs.title: Reporting
docs.text:
• Customers report through the web portal or the USSD menu.
  • Staff can log a report on behalf of a customer who phones or visits.
  • A report includes a type (leak, no water, meter problem, billing question, other), a description, and optionally a photo and location (portal only).

docs.title: Handling
docs.text:
Status Meaning Open Reported, not yet assigned Assigned A field officer has been assigned by a manager or by zone Resolved The field officer has fixed it and recorded notes and an optional photo

The customer receives an SMS when the report is assigned and when it is resolved.

Repair costs are recorded as expenses (see Expenses and funding). Leaks on main pipes are relevant to the water-loss report.

See Problem report workflow.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• PR-01 — Customer reporting: Customers can report problems through the portal and USSD.
  • PR-02 — Staff reporting: Staff can log a report for a customer.
  • PR-03 — Assignment: Managers can assign reports to field officers, or reports are routed by zone.
  • PR-04 — Status tracking: Reports move through Open, Assigned, and Resolved.
  • PR-05 — Resolution record: Field officers record notes and an optional photo when resolving.
  • PR-06 — Customer updates: Customers receive SMS updates on assignment and resolution.
  • PR-07 — Reporting: Open and resolved reports and average time to resolve are reported by zone.

docs.title: Questions to confirm
docs.text:
• Should reports have a priority, for example a burst main above a single meter fault?
  • Can a customer reopen a report they believe is not fixed?
  • Can members of the public who are not customers report a leak?

docs.title: Reports
docs.text:
Reports are for internal management — managers, accountants, committees, and org admins. Reports for regulators such as WASREB are out of scope.

All reports can be generated for a selected scheme and period, and exported to PDF (for committee meetings) and Excel (for accountants). Organizations with several schemes can also view reports across all their schemes side by side.

docs.title: Revenue and collections summary
docs.text: Total billed, total collected through M-Pesa by revenue category, donor and government funding, and outstanding unpaid balances.

docs.title: Profit and loss statement
docs.text: Revenue compared with operating costs by expense category.

docs.title: Unmatched payments
docs.text: M-Pesa payments still waiting to be matched by the accountant, with age.

docs.title: Customer statement
docs.text: One customer's bills, payments, credits, refunds, and balance over time. Used for disputes and tenant move-outs.

docs.title: Monthly progress and water-loss report
docs.text: Water produced at the source, water sold, active pumping days, and estimated water lost.

docs.title: Unread meters
docs.text: Meters with no reading in the period and the reason given. Meters blank several periods in a row are highlighted.

docs.title: Field action list
docs.text: Overdue accounts grouped by zone for follow-up, and accounts eligible for disconnection under the organization's rules.

docs.title: Disconnections and reconnections
docs.text: Pending approvals, completed disconnections, reconnections, and reconnection fees collected.

docs.title: Problem reports
docs.text: Open and resolved reports and average time to resolve, by zone.

docs.title: Customer compliance audit
docs.text: Customers who have not verified their phone accounts or whose signed contracts have not been uploaded.

docs.title: Property manager view
docs.text: Totals by building and unit, including empty units billed to the landlord.

docs.title: Organization-wide view
docs.text: For organizations with several schemes, such as counties: key figures for each scheme side by side.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• RP-01: Reports can be generated for a selected scheme and period.
  • RP-02: Reports include the measures described above.
  • RP-03: Reports can be exported to PDF and Excel.
  • RP-04: Overdue accounts can be grouped by zone.
  • RP-05: Verification and missing-contract exceptions can be identified.
  • RP-06: Unread meters and their reasons are reported.
  • RP-07: Unmatched payments are reported.
  • RP-08: A statement can be produced for any customer.
  • RP-09: Property managers can report by building and unit.
  • RP-10: Multi-scheme organizations can compare schemes side by side.
  • RP-11: Donor and government funding is shown separately from customer collections.
  • RP-12: Committee members can view and export reports but not change data.

docs.title: Questions to confirm
docs.text:
• What is the definition of "revenue" in the profit and loss report: amounts billed or amounts collected?
  • Which filters are required beyond scheme and period (zone, connection type, building)?
  • Should reports be sent automatically, for example a monthly PDF emailed to the committee?

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Each organization uses a fixed set of roles. Organizations cannot create custom roles. An org admin assigns roles to staff and assigns staff to schemes.

docs.title: Roles
docs.text: Role Scope Can do Platform admin Whole platform Onboard organizations, manage subscriptions, suspend and reactivate organizations, logged support access. See Platform administration. Org admin All schemes in the organization Configure schemes, tariffs, Paybills, policies, SMS sender name, expense categories; manage staff; pay the platform subscription; run data imports. Manager Assigned schemes Approve disconnections, correct readings, assign problem reports, add fines, send bulk SMS notices, review readings and reports. Field officer Assigned schemes Register customers, upload contracts, install meters, handle problem reports, carry out disconnections and reconnections, record tenant move-in and move-out. Meter reader Assigned routes Record readings and "not read" reasons for meters on assigned routes, including offline. Accountant Assigned schemes Record expenses and funding, match unmatched payments, record refunds, run financial reports. Committee member Assigned schemes Read-only access to reports and finances. Customer Own account View bills, consumption, and contracts; pay; report problems.

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
• Access is per scheme. Staff only see schemes they are assigned to.
  • One person can hold more than one role, for example meter reader and field officer in a small scheme.
  • Expenses are approved by the committee in its meetings, outside the system. The committee role remains read-only.
  • Sensitive actions are recorded in an audit log with who, when, and the reason: editing a reading, matching or reversing a payment, waiving or adding a fine, approving or carrying out a disconnection, editing or cancelling an expense, and platform admin support access.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• RL-01 — Fixed roles: The system provides the roles above; custom roles are not supported.
  • RL-02 — Multiple roles: A user can hold more than one role.
  • RL-03 — Scheme assignment: Staff roles apply only to assigned schemes; meter readers are further limited to assigned routes.
  • RL-04 — Committee read-only: Committee members cannot create or change data.
  • RL-05 — Audit log: Sensitive actions are logged and the log is visible to managers and org admins.

docs.title: Questions to confirm
docs.text:
• Can a user belong to more than one organization (for example, a contractor meter reader working for two schemes)?
  • Can an accountant reverse a payment, or only a manager?
  • Should committee members see individual customer details, or only totals?

docs.title: Customer registration workflow
docs.text: This workflow applies to community schemes, counties, and water service providers. For tenants of property managers, see Tenant move-in and move-out.

docs.title: Primary flow
docs.text:
1. The field officer selects the scheme they are assigned to.
  2. The field officer records the customer's details and connection type. Status: Applied.
  3. The system creates a customer account linked to the mobile number, and the customer receives an SMS verification code.
  4. The customer verifies the account and sets a password (portal), or uses USSD with their phone number.
  5. The customer pays the connection fee to the scheme's Paybill. Status: Fee paid.
  6. The customer signs the user agreement and, where required, land consent form. The field officer uploads them.
  7. The field officer installs the meter and records its serial number, starting reading, meter photo, and GPS location. Status: Installed.
  8. The connection becomes Active. The system will not activate it until the fee is paid and the contract uploaded.
  9. Billing starts from the starting reading.

docs.title: Expected outcome
docs.text: The customer belongs to the correct scheme, has an active connection with a starting reading, and can use the portal or USSD.

docs.title: Exceptions to define
docs.text:
• The phone number is already associated with an account.
  • SMS delivery fails or the verification code expires.
  • Required customer information is unavailable.
  • A contract is missing or an uploaded file cannot be read.
  • The customer pays the connection fee but the meter cannot be installed.

docs.title: Disconnection and reconnection workflow
docs.text: Applies only to organizations that enable a disconnection rule.

docs.title: Disconnection
docs.text:
1. An account becomes overdue beyond the organization's rule (days or amount).
  2. It appears on the field action list for its zone.
  3. A manager reviews and approves the disconnection, or leaves it.
  4. The customer receives a warning SMS.
  5. The field officer visits, disconnects, and records the meter reading and a photo.
  6. The connection status becomes Disconnected. It is no longer billed or counted for the subscription.

docs.title: Reconnection
docs.text:
1. The customer pays the overdue amount and the reconnection fee by M-Pesa.
  2. The account appears on the field officer's reconnection list.
  3. The field officer reconnects and records the meter reading.
  4. The connection status returns to Active and billing resumes from that reading.

docs.title: Exceptions to define
docs.text:
• The customer pays after approval but before the visit.
  • The field officer cannot access the meter.
  • A disconnected meter shows usage at the next visit (possible illegal reconnection).

docs.title: Online reading
docs.text:
1. The reader opens the app and selects an assigned route.
  2. The reader selects the meter.
  3. The app displays the previous reading.
  4. The reader enters the current reading and takes a photo of the meter.
  5. The app requests location permission and captures GPS coordinates when available.
  6. The system checks whether the reading is lower than the previous reading or an unusually large increase.
  7. The reader reviews any warning and submits.
  8. The system produces a bill and sends it by SMS.

docs.title: Meter cannot be read
docs.text:
1. The reader selects Not read and chooses a reason (locked gate, broken meter, obstructed, other).
  2. No bill and no standing fee are produced for the period.
  3. The meter appears on the unread meters report.
  4. The next real reading covers all usage since the last real reading.

docs.title: Offline reading
docs.text:
1. The reader records readings, photos, and not-read reasons without a network connection.
  2. They are saved on the phone.
  3. When connectivity returns, the app synchronizes them and bills are produced.

Offline conflict handling and synchronization status indicators still need to be designed.

docs.title: Main supply reading
docs.text: Readers also capture readings from the main source meter, such as a pumping station or tank. The system compares supplied water with water sold to estimate water loss.

docs.title: Expected flow
docs.text:
1. The customer pays from the portal or USSD (PIN prompt), or sends money directly to the scheme's Paybill with their account number.
  2. The system receives the M-Pesa transaction.
  3. If the transaction code has already been recorded, the duplicate is ignored.
  4. If the account number matches a customer in that scheme, the payment is recorded.
  5. The payment is allocated in the organization's configured order (default: fines, reconnection fees, overdue bills, current bill).
  6. Any remaining amount is kept as account credit.
  7. The customer receives an SMS receipt with the amount, M-Pesa code, and updated balance.

docs.title: Unmatched payment
docs.text:
1. The account number is wrong or missing, so the payment goes to the unmatched payments list.
  2. The accountant identifies the right customer, for example from the payer's name or phone number.
  3. The accountant matches the payment. The match is logged.
  4. Allocation and SMS receipt follow as above.

docs.title: Unresolved payment cases
docs.text: Handling of reversals and failed transactions still needs to be specified before the payment integration is implemented.

docs.title: Organization onboarding workflow
docs.text:
1. The platform admin creates the organization, sets its type and subscription plan, and creates the first org admin.
  2. The org admin sets up schemes, locations, zones or buildings, and each scheme's Paybill.
  3. The org admin sets tariffs (price per unit for each connection type, standing fee, flat rate), reading frequency, payment allocation order, and penalty and disconnection rules.
  4. The org admin sets the SMS sender name and expense categories.
  5. The org admin adds staff, assigns roles, and assigns them to schemes and routes.
  6. The org admin (or platform admin) downloads the Excel template, fills in customers, connections, meters, last readings, and opening balances, and uploads it.
  7. The system checks the file. Errors are fixed and the file re-uploaded until it is clean.
  8. Records are created. Customers receive SMS verification codes.
  9. Field officers upload contracts. Missing contracts appear in the customer compliance report.
  10. The first reading cycle produces the first bills.

docs.title: Exceptions to define
docs.text:
• The Paybill is not yet available when the organization wants to start.
  • The organization's records are too incomplete to import.

docs.title: Problem report workflow
docs.text:
1. The customer reports a problem through the portal or USSD, or staff log it for them. Status: Open.
  2. A manager assigns it to a field officer, or it is routed by zone. Status: Assigned. The customer receives an SMS.
  3. The field officer visits and fixes the problem.
  4. The field officer records notes and an optional photo. Status: Resolved. The customer receives an SMS.
  5. Any repair cost is recorded by the accountant as an expense.

docs.title: Exceptions to define
docs.text:
• The problem cannot be fixed on the first visit.
  • The report is a duplicate of an existing report.
  • The problem is the customer's responsibility, not the scheme's.

docs.title: Tenant move-in and move-out workflow
docs.text: Applies to property managers. The meter belongs to the unit; tenants come and go.

docs.title: Move-in
docs.text:
1. The field officer selects the building and unit.
  2. The field officer records the tenant's name and phone number.
  3. A move-in reading and meter photo are recorded.
  4. The tenant becomes the unit's account holder. Usage before the move-in reading stays with the previous account holder or the landlord.
  5. The tenant receives an SMS verification code and can use the portal or USSD.

docs.title: Monthly
docs.text: The unit's meter is read and billed to the tenant like any other connection. The tenant may never see the meter; every bill shows the previous reading, current reading, and units used, and the meter photo is visible in the portal.

docs.title: Move-out
docs.text:
1. The field officer records a move-out reading and photo.
  2. The system produces a final bill on the tenant's account.
  3. Any credit is applied to the final bill.
  4. Any remaining unpaid amount stays on the tenant's account, not the unit.
  5. Any remaining credit is refunded to the tenant by the accountant outside the system and recorded as a refund.
  6. The unit becomes empty.

docs.title: Empty unit
docs.text: While a unit is empty, its usage is billed to the landlord, until the next tenant's move-in reading.

docs.title: Exceptions to define
docs.text:
• The tenant leaves without notice and no move-out reading is taken.
  • The move-out reading cannot be taken because the unit is locked.
  • A tenant moves from one unit to another in the same building.
